summary: Backend auth cookie flow VERIFIED. All 3 requested features working: (1) POST /api/auth/login sets httpOnly session_token cookie with correct attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=none) and returns user payload, (2) GET /api/auth/me using cookie returns user profile without Authorization header, (3) POST /api/auth/google/logout clears session_token cookie without crash.
passed_tests: POST /api/auth/login returns 200 and sets session_token cookie
Login response contains access_token, user_id, email, name, tier, is_admin
GET /api/auth/me with cookie (no Authorization header) returns 200
/api/auth/me returns user profile with email, user_id, tier, is_admin

notes: Returns 200 with user payload (access_token, user_id, email, name, tier, is_admin)
Sets session_token cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=none, Path=/, Max-Age=2592000 (30 days)
Returns 200 with user profile when session_token cookie is present
No Authorization header required - cookie-only authentication works
Returns email, user_id, tier, is_admin, accepted_terms, etc.
Clears session_token cookie by setting Max-Age=0

critical_code_review_comments: Cookie attributes correctly set: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=none - good for cross-origin requests
auth.py get_current_user() correctly checks cookie first, then Authorization header - proper fallback
Logout endpoint correctly deletes session from user_sessions collection and clears cookie
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth cookie flow verified working. Login sets httpOnly session_token cookie, /api/auth/me works with cookie-only auth (no Authorization header needed), logout clears cookie. Frontend uses credentials: 'include' in api.js for cookie handling. Google OAuth session endpoint also sets cookie correctly.
